performed_via_github_app.name: changeset-bot
performed_via_github_app.description: This bot will comment on PRs saying that either a user might need to add a changeset(note that PRs changing things like documentation generally don't need a changeset)or say that the PR is good and already has a changeset. Sometimes, a contributor won't add a changeset to a PR but you might want to merge in the PR without having to wait on them to add it. To address this, this bot adds a link with the filename pre-filled to add a changeset so all you have to do is write the changeset and click commit. When writing the changeset, it should look something like this with the packages that are being released in the YAML front matter with associated semver bump types and the summary of the changes in markdown. ```markdown --- '@changesets/cli': major '@changesets/read': minor --- A very helpful description of the changes ```

performed_via_github_app.description:
## What is [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io)?
CodSpeed is a **continuous benchmarking** platform that allows you to **track** and **compare** the **performance** of your codebase during development.

It uses a smart **runtime engine** to measure the performance of your code in an **accurate** and **reproducible** way without creating a huge **runtime overhead**, unlike traditional benchmarks.

CodSpeed produces detailed **performance reports** helping you **improve** your codebase **performance**, directly **within your repository provider** (Pull Requests comments, Merge checks, ...).

## How it works

The core of the **performance measurement** is done directly within your **CI environment** through the **CodSpeed Action**. Allowing you to **stay the sole owner** of your data and to keep your **codebase private**.

Once the performance data is generated, **only the benchmark results** are sent to the CodSpeed servers to be **analyzed**.

Then, performance reports are **generated** and **published** directly **within your repository provider**.

## How long does it take to install?

If you're **already benchmarking** your codebase, you can plug your **existing benchmarks** to CodSpeed in **less than 5 minutes** since CodSpeed benchmark's API is **compatible** with the most **popular benchmarking frameworks**.

If **you haven't any benchmarks yet**, we provide an **intuitive** benchmarking API that allows you to **create your first benchmarks** in a **few minutes**.

This is for sure not done yet, but the changes in the core and node lib seem to be functional in the example project. Therefore I wanted to check in what you think of the direction I'm taking, before I start streamlining/cleaning things up, writing docs, etc.
@ematipico what do you think? Thanks 🙏
Hello! We require new features to be accepted through our RFC process in https://github.com/withastro/roadmap/ first, so I’m closing this until the discussions there are concluded.

For this it's not necessary, and I already spoke with @leekeh  about this feature and it was ok to land it. It's an enhancement of something we already have, so an RFC isn't needed

Sorry about that, I didn't have that context. Thanks for reopening @ematipico and thanks for the work @leekeh!

Thanks and no worries! I will try to put some more effort into this one soon also 🙏  Initial feedback is already welcome :)

@leekeh I ran an automated review against this feature. It's made with an AI, so take the findings with a pinch of salt. For example I think the second bullet point is false positive. Version are bumped automatically via changsets

## Findings

- `[high][security]` `packages/integrations/node/src/serve-app.ts:26` - `staticAssetPath` is attacker-derived and joined without verifying it remains inside `client`. A doubly encoded traversal path matched by a prerendered catch-all can read matching `.html` files outside `dist/client`. Reuse the containment protection from `resolveStaticPath()` before opening the file.

- `[high][runtime]` `packages/integrations/node/src/serve-app.ts:5` - The adapter unconditionally imports the newly added `getStaticAssetPath`, but its peer dependency remains `astro: ^7.0.0`. Updating only `@astrojs/node` will break Astro 7.0/7.1 applications because those versions lack this export, even in classic mode. Raise the Astro peer minimum to the release introducing this API.

- `[high][completeness]` `packages/astro/src/types/public/integrations.ts:84` - Widening the shared `MiddlewareMode` also makes Netlify and Vercel accept `'on-request'`. Neither adapter routes prerendered assets through SSR or provides `getStaticAsset`, so middleware is skipped both during build and at request time. Authentication middleware can therefore be silently bypassed. Narrow their option types until they implement the mode.

- `[medium][correctness]` `packages/integrations/node/src/serve-app.ts:93` - Static output paths are derived incorrectly. The supplied pathname is already base-stripped, so routes beginning with the configured base are stripped twice. Additionally, ignoring `routeData.isIndex` makes `build.format: 'preserve'` read `blog.html` for `src/pages/blog/index.astro`, whose output is `blog/index.html`. Derive paths using the route metadata and the canonical build mapping.

- `[medium][correctness]` `packages/integrations/node/src/serve-app.ts:145` - SSR-to-prerender rewrites cannot work in production. Node only supplies `getStaticAsset` when the initial route is prerendered, and `AppPipeline.tryRewrite()` attempts to load the prerendered target from the SSR `pageMap`, which deliberately excludes it. The unit test masks both conditions by injecting the callback and target module manually.

- `[medium][correctness]` `packages/astro/src/core/routing/rewrite.ts:162` - `includeHeaders` does not preserve request data. `createRequest()` still receives `isPrerendered: true` without `preserveRequestData`, causing headers, cookies, body, and query parameters to be stripped during string/URL rewrites to prerendered routes.

- `[medium][error-handling]` `packages/integrations/node/src/serve-app.ts:35` - Every file-open failure is treated as a missing asset. Permission errors, descriptor exhaustion, and I/O failures consequently become misleading 404 responses. Only expected missing-file errors should return `undefined`; other errors should propagate to Astro's 500 handling.

- `[low][completeness]` `packages/integrations/node/src/types.ts:25` - `experimentalErrorPageHost` is reintroduced in the public type but is never used. This option was deliberately removed in `@astrojs/node` 10.0.0, so configuration is accepted without effect. Remove it again.

- `[low][documentation]` `packages/astro/src/core/pages/handler.ts:114` - New comments here and in `core/rewrites/handler.ts:52` mention an `"always"` middleware mode that does not exist. They should refer only to `"on-request"`.
